title: Every Door
concept: At UAA the AI rule hangs on each classroom door behind one handbook sentence that never says AI, so the film makes the rule a row of doors that all carry the SAME coral AI glyph with a different navy verdict mark at every one, and asks whether November's guiding principles should add one shared default.

fingerprint.palette: friendly fluorescent seafoam corridor, dusty-blue lockers, plum doors, navy ink, a single coral glyph mark that only ever means an AI rule applied or counted, playful and saturated
fingerprint.metaphor: a hallway of identical doors where the same AI sign carries a different verdict at every one

palette: friendly fluorescent seafoam corridor, dusty-blue lockers, plum doors, navy ink, a single coral glyph mark that only ever means an AI rule applied or counted, playful and saturated
divergence_note: First fluorescent interior in three. 10-03 was daylight newsprint cream and spruce in a newsroom with a vertical rise and an amber accent, 10-02 a night lamplit brass bench in cross-section. This one is a cool seafoam hallway under tube light with plum doors, dusty-blue lockers and nickel hardware, one coral accent that only ever means an AI rule applied or counted, and a camera that travels sideways in parallax past a row of doors instead of rising. The desk and plate inserts of 10-02 are not reused: the report desk, regents table and syllabus page are lit by cool tube and pendant light with no brass, no tally counter and no lamp pool. New hero (ClassroomDoor), new throughline (the coral glyph and its verdict marks), new sets (corridor, handbook plate wall, locker wall and dot field, report desk, boardroom table, writing classroom, lab, syllabus page).

angle.thesis: At UAA the AI rule lives in each instructor's syllabus, behind one handbook sentence about devices that never mentions AI, so a count of 119 AI cases of 150 measures how often the rule was invoked more than how much students use AI, and November's guiding principles can at best give every syllabus a shared starting point.
angle.falsifiability: False if the November document turns out to be a binding systemwide AI conduct rule, if UAA has a separate written AI conduct rule outside the handbook section, or if ADN or the report shows the 119 cases were decided under one named AI standard.
supporting_facts: c6 + c7 no single UA-wide AI rule, the handbook bars devices not authorized by the faculty member and never mentions AI
c1 + c2 + c8 119 of 150 cited used AI, 1.1% of 10,500+ students, the report says AI cases have taken over the majority
c4 + c5 regents will consider guiding principles in November, draft language went to them in September
angle.counter_point: Course by course may be the right design, since AI use that's cheating in a composition course is the assignment in UAA's own graduate AI program (c12). And the numbers are real: AI plagiarism rose 73% last year (c3), and waiting for perfect definitions is the 'just happen to us' failure Erickson names (c9).
angle.second_movement: c12 recontextualises the first: the same university teaches AI as a graduate discipline, so the mismatch is inside one institution. The principles will be a shared starting point and still not a rule, and the honest question is whether one default helps or the course-by-course door fits better.

runner_ups.angle: Enthusiast: November is the Alaska win
runner_ups.why_lost: the facts don't say what the principles contain, so the win is a hope, not a finding; folded in as the counter-point

runner_ups.angle: Skeptic: the number measures enforcement not use
runner_ups.why_lost: strongest on the numbers but implies doubt about a report we can't see; folded in as the 1.1% turn with attribution

angle.close_question: When regents take up AI principles in November, should UA set one default for authorized AI use or keep the call with each faculty member?
angle.challenge_round: Three proposals converged on the same facts. Challenges: enthusiast's 'Alaska win' asserts what the principles say (unsupported, demoted); skeptic's 'measures enforcement' reads the report's intent (unsupported, softened to 'counts citations'); explainer is the most falsifiable and gives the film a picture (doors and signs). Synthesis: explainer thesis, skeptic's 1.1% turn, enthusiast's graduate-program counterpoint.

treatment.why: Cleanest mechanism picture (one sentence over a row of doors, the same glyph with a different verdict at each), a locker-field pullback that makes 1.1% felt without implying innocence, and the fairest Test (two doors, one tool, opposite answers, a key that jams in both).
grafts: COMEDIAN Raven cocking its head at the empty dashed box
DRAMATIST the slips as the real pressure at full volume and the unnailed hook for the not-a-rule line
ENTHUSIAST the last door opening onto warm light as the loop payoff

hook.frame1: A dark hallway of shut doors, one tube ticking, then the tubes clang on and each door lamp blinks.
hook.headline: NO SYSTEMWIDE AI RULE
hook.loopback: The tubes click off to the single ticking tube of frame 1, the dashed box is the last thing lit, and the film ends where it began.

open_loop.what: The dark shut door at the far end of the row, shown with a coral arrow in the opening wide view at 17 s and held centered at 22 s, opens at 85 s onto UAA's master's program in AI where AI is the subject.

open_loop_2.what: The taped folder with the coral glyph on its cover, planted at 57 s with a draft inside, is opened at 100 s to a REGENTS · NOVEMBER plate and a guiding principles scroll.
